Hi Sarah — great questions and totally reasonable constraints. I attached a concise options summary and a proposal PDF that lays out two commercial options and the standard legal positions we usually take on prepay refunds/termination. High level below:

Option A — 12-month annual prepay (preferred for flexibility)
- Commitment: $250,000 annual prepayment (billed up front)
- Prepay discount: 10% off list for the year (effective price $225,000)
- Early termination: pro-rata credit for unused months less a termination fee equal to 15% of the remaining prorated committed value; standard 30-day notice.
- Co-terming: allowed with proration; no additional fee if co-term date within first 90 days of renewal.

Option B — 36-month multi-year prepay (best unit economics)
- Commitment: 3 x $250,000 = $750,000 prepay up front
- Multi-year discount: 20% aggregate discount across the term (effective total $600,000; ~equivalent to 1 - (1 - 0.2) pro-rata)
- Ramp schedule: Year1 reserved baseline capacity = 60% of committed throughput, Year2 = 80%, Year3 = 100%; unused reserved capacity can be converted to token credits redeemable for other Redwood services within the term.
- Early termination: refund equal to remaining unused prepay value prorated by leftover term, less an early termination charge equal to 10% of the remaining committed value. No refunds within first 90 days of initial term for multi-year prepay.
- Co-terming: we can co-term in year 2 with a one-time credits adjustment that preserves economic value (see proposed redline).

Attached: Redwood_Proposal_Aster_20260302.pdf (includes a sample SOW & high-level redline language).

If these look OK, I can loop in Legal (Rishi) and our SE (Connor) to prepare a negotiated SOW and redline.

Best,

Marissa — see inline guidance and suggested redline language below. High-level position: we are willing to offer refunds for unused prepay on multi-year deals with a conservative termination charge to mitigate resale risk. Co-terming is acceptable subject to preserving seller economics via a crediting formula.

Suggested redline snippets (to include in SOW/SaaS Agreement):
- Termination for convenience: Customer may terminate for convenience after the initial 90-day period by providing 60 days' written notice. Refunds (if any) will be calculated as: (Remaining full months in term / Total months in term) * Prepaid Amount, less an early termination charge equal to 10% of the Remaining Prepaid Amount.
- No refunds available for termination within the first 90 days of the initial term for multi-year prepay.
- Co-terming: If the Parties agree to align the Agreement to Customer's fiscal year mid-term, Seller will apply a one-time Co-Term Credit equal to the prorated Remaining Prepaid Amount, applied toward the new co-term, less any applicable early termination charge per the formula above. Co-Term Credit may be used only toward Redwood services and expires at the end of the new co-term.
- Ramp/Unused Capacity: Seller will convert unused reserved capacity to Redwood service credits at fair market value (FMV) as calculated by Seller's internal conversion table (to be shared in SOW). Credits are valid for use within the existing term and may be used for overages on other Redwood routes but are not refundable in cash.

Attachments: I drafted a redlined SOW that incorporates the above: SOW_Redlined_20260305.docx. Please review and let me know if Sales wants any commercial flex — specifically the termination charge percentage or onboarding credit.

-Rishi

Sarah — appreciate the clarity and the asks. We can take the following positions to get to a clean mark for signature:

1) Termination charge: we can make the termination charge fungible as a Redwood credit instead of withholding a cash refund. The credit will be applied per the same calculation (Remaining months / Total months * Prepaid Amount) less 10% charge and will be redeemable for Redwood services or for third-party services procured through Redwood's partner integrations (we will list eligible partner vendors in the SOW appendix).

2) Co-terming: we will allow co-term alignment in year 2 with a one-time Co-Term Credit as drafted by Rishi. The Co-Term Credit will be applicable against eligible Redwood or partner services.

3) Ramp conversion table: Connor will produce an illustrative conversion table (GPU-hour equivalence to token-credit) and share it in the SOW appendix; for now we will include a formula-based description: Unused reserved capacity in a month = (Committed reserved capacity - Actual consumption) which is converted to credits at a 1:1 token-equivalent conversion defined in Appendix A. Connor will follow up with the sample table by EOD tomorrow.

4) Onboarding credit & SLA: We can include a one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 for the 3-year prepay and agree to an SLA credit capped at 5% of the quarterly prepaid amount for missed SLA (subject to standard SLA definitions / remediation windows).

Next steps: Rishi — please incorporate the agreed credit fungibility and partner eligibility language into the redline. Neha/Connor — confirm the onboarding credit and conversion table items. Sarah — once we have the updated SOW redline and conversion table, I will circulate a DocuSign for Aster to sign.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Marissa
